RS.regel: Learn the tricky words: definitely, independent, develop, lose (verlieren) – loose (locker), a lot (two words), cannot (one word), which, babies. After a full stop, always start with a capital letter. Merke: Nach dem Punkt groß weiter!

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the correct spelling.
items: Many young people want to become (independant / independent) of their parents.
She was (definitely / definately) influenced by her older sister.
It takes time to (develope / develop) a stable identity.
Some teenagers are afraid to (loose / lose) their friends if they act differently.
Influencers post (alot / a lot) of photos every day.

uebungen.auftrag: Find the spelling mistake in each sentence and correct it. One sentence is correct.
items: As ⟦babys⟧, people learn whether they can trust others.
Teenagers ⟦can not⟧ always decide who they want to be.
The article explains a theory ⟦wich⟧ is easy to understand.
The text is short. ⟦it⟧ is written for young readers.
Peer pressure can make you ⟦loose⟧ your confidence.
The author clearly addresses young people.

KOM.regel: Use a comma after introductory words and phrases (Furthermore, … / In my opinion, … / For example, …). Use commas around non-defining relative clauses (Erikson's idea of fidelity, which …). Do NOT put a comma before 'because' or 'that', and not around defining relative clauses (Teenagers who … feel …). Merke: Englisch setzt viel weniger Kommas als Deutsch – außer nach Einleitungswörtern.

uebungen.auftrag: Add a comma where it is needed.
items: Furthermore the author uses a lot of questions.
In my opinion social media has changed the way teenagers see themselves.
For example the writer speaks to the reader directly.
According to the psychologist every stage of life has its own task.
According to the psychologist, every stage …
All in all the text is easy to read.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the punctuation: add or delete commas (or full stops). One sentence is correct.
items: Young people feel insecure⟦,⟧ because they compare themselves with others.
Teenagers⟦,⟧ who spend hours online⟦,⟧ often feel worse about themselves.
The writer believes⟦,⟧ that identity takes time.
The text describes fidelity which is the ability to stay true to yourself.
Many apps show edited pictures⟦.⟧ that look perfect.
no full stop: pictures that look perfect
Moreover, the author uses an enumeration.

VW.titel: Words that sound alike: their / there / they're, its / it's, then / than, whose / who's, to / too
VW.regel: their = ihr/e (their values) · there = dort / there is, there are · its = sein/ihr (its own challenge) · it's = it is · then = dann · than = als (more than) · whose = dessen/deren · who's = who is · too = zu (too many). Merke: Kannst du 'it is' sagen? Dann it's.

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the correct word.
items: Teenagers often struggle to find (their / there) place in the world.
(Their / There) are many voices that tell young people what to do.
Every stage of life has (its / it's) own task.
Life online seems more exciting (then / than) real life.
Some young people feel there are (to / too) many expectations.

uebungen.auftrag: Find the mistake and correct it. One sentence is correct.
items: ⟦Its⟧ hard to know who you really are at fifteen.
A teenager ⟦who's⟧ self-image is fragile needs support.
They try to copy ⟦there⟧ favourite influencers.
Today you get more advice online ⟦then⟧ from your family.
⟦Their⟧ is no easy answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
It's normal to feel confused at this age.

ART.regel: an before a vowel sound (an informal tone, an enumeration). No article with general uncountable nouns: self-esteem, life, adolescence, language (He uses informal language). Use a/an with jobs and roles: as a baby, as a child, he is a psychologist. Merke: Allgemeine Begriffe ohne 'the'.

uebungen.auftrag: Fill in a, an or – (no article).
items: The author uses ___ enumeration to show the pressure.
People with a strong identity have higher ___ self-esteem.
As ___ child, you learn to be independent.
___ adolescence is a time of change.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the article mistakes. One sentence is correct.
items: Each phase of ⟦the life⟧ has its own problems.
In ⟦the adolescence⟧ young people ask who they are.
Teenagers with ⟦a⟧ better self-esteem worry less.
⟦The social media⟧ shows only the best moments.
As a baby, you learn whether you can trust people.

PRAEP.regel: agree with sb/sth · depend on · suffer from · be interested in · on the internet · compare A to/with B · relatable to · speak to sb · published in 2026 / on 10 July · for + Zeitraum (for years), since + Zeitpunkt (since 2020). Merke: Präpositionen als Paket mit dem Verb lernen!

uebungen.auftrag: Fill in the correct preposition.
items: Many teenagers depend ___ the opinions of their friends.
Some young people suffer ___ low self-esteem.
Many fans are interested ___ fashion trends.
My cousin found a great video ___ the internet.

uebungen.auftrag: Find the wrong preposition and correct it. One sentence is correct.
items: She has used Instagram ⟦since⟧ three years.
The writer speaks ⟦with⟧ the reader like a friend.
The examples are relatable ⟦for⟧ most students.

TEMP.titel: Simple present vs. progressive vs. present perfect
TEMP.regel: When you write about a text, use the simple present: The author uses / lists / explains. Facts and habits: Babies learn to trust. Present perfect (progressive) for 'seit': They have been using social media since they were twelve. Merke: Textanalyse = simple present, kein -ing!

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the correct form.
items: In the third paragraph, the author (is listing / lists) several influences.
Toddlers (are learning / learn) to walk around the age of one.
In the last paragraph, the author (is addressing / addresses) young people.
Many teenagers (use / have used) social media since they were eleven.
The text (is explaining / explains) a psychological theory.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the verb forms if necessary. One sentence is correct.
items: In line 23, the writer ⟦is using⟧ an image.
Teenagers ⟦are using⟧ smartphones since primary school.
The examples which ⟦are illustrating⟧ the problem appear in the last paragraph.
Erikson ⟦has explained⟧ that each stage has a task (summary of the text).
The tag question imitates spoken language.

SVA.titel: He, she, it – das s muss mit
SVA.regel: Third person singular in the simple present needs -s: the author uses, he says, every influencer says, the text shows. Who/which + singular → -s; plural → no -s: people who know, people who have. Merke: He, she, it – das s muss mit!

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the correct form.
items: Erikson (say / says) that every stage has a challenge.
Every teenager (want / wants) to be accepted.
People who (has / have) a strong identity feel calmer.
This example (show / shows) how confusing the situation is.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the verb if necessary. One sentence is correct.
items: Because of the question, the reader ⟦feel⟧ involved.
A student who ⟦know⟧ the answer raises her hand.
Teenagers who compare themselves with others often feel worse.

REG.titel: Formal register in analysis and comment
REG.regel: Avoid spoken English in a Klausur: really/pretty → very, rather; a lot (of) → many, much, frequently; way more → far more; stuff → aspects, devices; don't/you'd → do not / you would. Merke: Schreib so, wie es in einer Zeitung stehen würde.

uebungen.auftrag: Replace the informal word(s) in brackets with a formal expression.
items: The topic is (pretty hard) to understand.
The website offers (a lot of stuff) for students.
Today there are (way more) apps than ten years ago.
The text is (really) easy to read.

uebungen.auftrag: Rewrite the sentences in a formal register. One sentence is already formal.
items: The writer's question sounds like something you'd hear at a party.
… something one would hear at a party.
The opening makes readers feel like it's all about them.
The opening makes readers feel personally addressed.
Teenagers get tons of opinions online.
The author's tone is super casual.
The author's tone is very informal.
Online comments don't bother them as much.
Online comments do not bother them as much.
The author deliberately chooses a conversational tone.

SB.regel: Two main clauses cannot be joined with a comma only. Use a full stop, a semicolon, a colon or a linking word: … is difficult. Many people … / … is difficult because many people … Merke: Hauptsatz, Hauptsatz – das geht im Englischen nicht mit Komma.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the comma splice. Use a full stop, a semicolon or 'because'.
items: Growing up is difficult, there are so many changes.
The text is easy to read, it uses everyday words.
Many people post only their best moments, others feel worse.
The tag question has a clear function, it involves the reader.
Teenagers feel lost, they do not know which way to go.

uebungen.auftrag: Find the comma splices and correct them. One sentence is correct; one needs 'there are'.
items: Some teenagers feel torn, this is a typical problem at that age.
In big cities are many opportunities.
The list is long, this shows how many people influence teenagers.
At school we learn facts, at home we learn values.
Confident people make clear choices, they listen less to gossip.
Because there are so many voices, it is easy to feel confused.

VERB.titel: Verb forms: negation, gerund and infinitive, passive
VERB.regel: Negation needs do/does: they don't know (not: they not know). I agree (not: I am agree). After avoid, instead of, without: -ing (avoid using, instead of discovering). Passive: this is called role confusion. Merke: Verneinung immer mit do/does + not.

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the correct form.
items: Many teenagers (not know / do not know) what they want.
My friends (agree / are agree) with me.
Many teens avoid (to talk / talking) about their worries.
Some people scroll instead of (do / doing) their homework.
This stage of life (calls / is called) adolescence.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the verb forms. One sentence is correct.
items: If you ⟦not like⟧ a photo, you delete it.
We ⟦are agree⟧ that social media has an influence.
He copies his older brother instead ⟦to try⟧ new hobbies.
Erikson's fifth stage ⟦calls⟧ 'identity versus role confusion'.
The writer avoids ⟦to give⟧ complicated examples.
Teenagers who do not know which way to go often feel overwhelmed.

WW.regel: develop an identity / fidelity (not: become), whether (ob, bei Alternativen) instead of if, look the same (not: look like the same), be prone to depression. Merke: Wörter in festen Verbindungen lernen.

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the better word.
items: Babies learn (whether / weather) the world is safe.
Many girls want to look (like the same / the same) as models.
The poem (is from / was written by) a young author.
Teenagers with a weak identity are more (prone / near) to anxiety.

uebungen.auftrag: Replace the word that does not fit. One sentence is correct.
items: Adolescents who succeed ⟦become⟧ a strong identity.
Children learn ⟦if⟧ they can rely on others.
Many fans try to look ⟦like the same⟧ as pop stars.
The author ⟦makes⟧ a metaphor in line 23.
A strong identity makes decisions easier.

KOMP.regel: Short adjectives: easy – easier – the easiest, happy – happier, bad – worse – the worst. Never 'more' + -er (not: more easy, more worse, more harder). Some adjectives are not compared: perfect, right. Merke: Entweder -er oder more – nie beides.

uebungen.auftrag: Write the correct comparative.
items: easy → The image makes the idea ___ to understand.
bad → Some teenagers think their life is ___ than others'.
happy → People with a strong identity are often ___.
hard → Social media makes it ___ to find yourself.
confusing → Life online is ___ than life offline.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the comparison. One sentence is correct.
items: A good example makes a rule ⟦more easy⟧ to remember.
They think their own body is ⟦more worse⟧.
It has become ⟦more harder⟧ to know who you are.
Teenagers with high self-esteem are ⟦more happy⟧.
Social media makes the search for identity more complex.

FF.regel: Handy = mobile phone / smartphone · eine eigene Identität = one's own identity / an identity of one's own (not: an own) · seit Jahren = for years · etwas anderes = something different / something else · something other ✗. Merke: Nicht Wort für Wort übersetzen!

uebungen.auftrag: Translate the German words in brackets.
items: It is important to find (eine eigene Identität).
She has been on TikTok (seit Jahren).
Each friend gives you (etwas anderes) to think about.
Teenagers want to find (ihren eigenen Weg).

uebungen.auftrag: Find the German-English mistake and correct it. One sentence is correct.
items: Most young people check their ⟦handy⟧ every few minutes.
Each website tells you ⟦something other⟧ about healthy food.
They have followed this influencer ⟦since⟧ two years.
It is hard to find ⟦the own⟧ way.
Everyone needs an identity of their own.

WF.regel: this picture – these pictures · thousands of messages · lines 24–26 (plural) · criticism (Kritik) – a critic (Kritiker) · teenagers → their (not: her). Merke: Plural auch bei this/these und bei Zahlen-Wörtern beachten.

uebungen.auftrag: Choose the correct form.
items: Look at (this / these) comments under the post.
The video got (thousand / thousands) of views.
The enumeration can be found in (line / lines) 24–26.
A strong identity protects you against (critic / criticism).
Teenagers often hide (her / their) real feelings.

uebungen.auftrag: Correct the word form. One sentence is correct.
items: She gets ⟦hundred⟧ of likes every day.
A good friend helps you deal with ⟦critic⟧.
Teenagers try to find ⟦her⟧ place in society.
